/speckit-specify Build a command-line bookmark manager that stores bookmarks in an SQLite database.

Run it as `python -m bookmarks [--db PATH] COMMAND ...`. The database is the file PATH, or `bookmarks.db` in the current directory when `--db` is not given. It is created if it does not exist, and bookmarks persist between runs.

Commands:

- `add URL [--title TITLE] [--tags TAGS]` adds a bookmark and prints its numeric id. Ids start at 1 and increase. The URL must start with `http://` or `https://`; anything else is rejected with an error message on standard error and exit status 2. TITLE defaults to an empty string. TAGS is a comma-separated list such as `python,cli`.
- `list [--tag TAG]` prints all bookmarks, or only those that have the tag TAG, ordered by id.
- `search TEXT` prints the bookmarks whose title or URL contains TEXT, ignoring case, ordered by id.
- `delete ID` deletes the bookmark with that id. If there is no such bookmark it prints an error message on standard error and exits with status 3.
- `export --format csv` prints all bookmarks as CSV with the header row `id,url,title,tags`. `export --format json` prints them as a JSON array of objects with the keys `id` (a number), `url`, `title` and `tags` (a list of strings).

`list` and `search` print one bookmark per line as four tab-separated fields: the id, the URL, the title, and the bookmark's tags joined with commas in alphabetical order. In CSV output, the tags field also holds the tags joined with commas in alphabetical order.

Successful commands exit with status 0.

Use Python 3.11 or newer and the standard library only (`sqlite3` is part of it). Put the code in a package named `bookmarks` under `src/`, so that it runs with `python -m bookmarks` when `src/` is on `PYTHONPATH`.

Examples (`<TAB>` stands for a tab character):

```
$ python -m bookmarks --db b.db add https://docs.python.org --title "Python docs" --tags python,docs
1
$ python -m bookmarks --db b.db add https://example.com
2
$ python -m bookmarks --db b.db list
1<TAB>https://docs.python.org<TAB>Python docs<TAB>docs,python
2<TAB>https://example.com<TAB><TAB>
$ python -m bookmarks --db b.db search PYTHON
1<TAB>https://docs.python.org<TAB>Python docs<TAB>docs,python
$ python -m bookmarks --db b.db add ftp://example.com
(an error message on standard error; exit status 2)
```

## Completion Report

- **SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY**: `specs/001-bookmark-cli-manager`
- **SPEC_FILE**: `specs/001-bookmark-cli-manager/spec.md`
- **Checklist**: `specs/001-bookmark-cli-manager/checklists/requirements.md` — 16/16 items pass on the first validation pass, with two noted items (see below)
- **Branch**: `001-bookmark-cli-manager` (created by the mandatory `before_specify` git hook; FEATURE_NUM `001`)
- **Pointer**: `.specify/feature.json` now records the feature directory for downstream commands

**What the spec contains**: four prioritized, independently testable user stories (P1 capture+recall, P2 search/tag filter, P3 delete, P4 export), 11 edge cases, 23 functional requirements grouped by command, three key entities, 7 measurable success criteria, and an assumptions section separating chosen defaults from requester/constitution constraints.

**Two things to know:**

1. The checklist's "no implementation details" items pass with a recorded exception. For a CLI, the invocation form, exit statuses and output formats *are* the user interface, so `python -m bookmarks …`, exit 2/3 and the tab/CSV/JSON formats sit in the requirements. The genuine solution constraints you mandated — Python 3.11+, standard library only, SQLite, `src/bookmarks` layout — are confined to the last block of the Assumptions section and kept out of the requirements and success criteria.

2. Your description left two details open; I settled both as documented decisions rather than blocking questions, since each has a clear default and neither shifts scope:
   - **Ids are never reused.** Delete the highest id and the next `add` takes a still-higher number, so a printed id stays a stable reference. (The naive SQLite rowid behaviour would recycle it.)
   - **Duplicate URLs are allowed** as distinct bookmarks; no deduplication.

   I also fixed the URL check as a literal, case-sensitive prefix test, so `HTTPS://example.com` is rejected with status 2 — worth a glance, as it's the one place a strict reading could surprise a user. Say the word if any of these should flip.

**Next**: ready for `/speckit-plan`. `/speckit-clarify` is available but has nothing to resolve — there are no `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` markers.
